outcome_summary: NEITHER cell reaches state 4 (COMMUTATE_HIGH_TO_ZVS, R04E21's own stall point) or state 5. Both cells park one state EARLIER, at state 3 (LOW_BUILD_NEGATIVE), at TSTOP=20us, because I_LIMIT=125A (vs R04E21's I_LIMIT=10A) changes the post-zero-crossing negative-current-build rate: IL1 only reaches -2.21509122849A by t=20us in both cells, which is LESS negative than BOTH swept I_NEG targets (2.5A for NEG_FRAC=.02, 9.7125A for NEG_FRAC=.0777), so the 3->4 transition rule (I(L1)<=-I_NEG) never fires in either cell. Because this rule never fires, the two cells' entire measured trajectory (all .meas values, IL1_MIN/IL1_MAX, VC1-3_FINAL, VOUT_FINAL) is numerically IDENTICAL between the two NEG_FRAC values -- NEG_FRAC has no effect on the observed physics under this TSTOP=20us window. The diagnosed R04E21 hypothesis (I_LIMIT/I_NEG rescaling) is therefore UNTESTED, not confirmed or refuted, by this specific netlist/TSTOP=20us combination -- the run never reaches the state-4 blocking condition R04E21 documented, so whether a rescaled I_NEG would unblock it cannot be determined from this data.

outcome_classification.reasoning: Both cells park at state 3 (LOW_BUILD_NEGATIVE) at TSTOP=20us, one state EARLIER than R04E21's own documented state-4 (COMMUTATE_HIGH_TO_ZVS) stall. Raising I_LIMIT from R04E3/R04E21's own 10A to P24's own locked 125A does exactly what BOUNDARY.md Section 2 predicted to state 0 (ENERGY dwells and charges further, t_energy_end=6.37ns vs R04E21's ~0.3ps), and the zero-crossing timing (t_il1_zero=1.632us) is close to R04E21's own (1.631us) -- but the previously-unexamined knock-on effect is that the POST-zero-crossing negative-current-build rate (state 3, LOW_BUILD_NEGATIVE) is far slower under this larger-I_LIMIT trajectory than under R04E21's: only -2.215A is reached by t=20us, versus R04E21's own -0.2A reached in just ~56ns after crossing zero. TSTOP=20us, inherited byte-identical from R04E3/R04E21 per this experiment's own stated scope, is not long enough for IL1 to reach EITHER swept I_NEG target (2.5A or 9.7125A) under this new trajectory. Because neither target is reached, NEG_FRAC has zero observed effect and both cells' full measured state is numerically identical. The specific question this experiment set out to answer (BOUNDARY.md Section 6: does a rescaled I_NEG unblock the state-4 ZVS event) is therefore UNTESTED by this run -- state 4 itself is never reached in either cell, so nothing can be concluded about whether the high-side ZVS event would or would not occur once it is.
